tasks.short: Prepare job classifications, job descriptions and salary scales.

steps.what: Retrieve the job request, position records and existing classification.
Collect relevant benchmark tables and approved evaluation guidance.
Interview the manager and job holder about responsibilities, scope and working conditions.
Write the job description using confirmed job facts and standard sections.

loop.input: Confirmed job facts, interview notes and approved description template.
loop.output: Draft description with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections; the specialist checks factual support and gender-neutral wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting facts return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot reliably turn varied interview notes into clear, faithful descriptions.

steps.what: Evaluate job factors and recommend a classification using the approved framework.
Calculate proposed salary ranges and check internal relativities and benchmark fit.
Approve the description, classification and salary scales after resolving exceptions.
Publish approved descriptions and update effective-dated classifications and salary scales.

tasks.design: An integration reads position records from the {HCM} and assembles licensed benchmarks and approved guidance from the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares descriptions, while deterministic calculations produce salary ranges and exception checks; specialists evaluate jobs and the manager approves changes. The {WORKFLOW} then publishes only the approved versions to the {HCM} and {DOCS}, with effective dates and an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job facts, benchmark licences and evaluation frameworks differ. Standard forms reduce typing but do not resolve contested job scope.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce the effort of building adapters, calculation tools and document generation. Bounded drafting can turn confirmed notes into a consistent description.
tasks.still_hard: Benchmark matching and gender-neutral factor interpretation need expertise. Assess GDPR and EU AI Act obligations if the tool influences employment decisions; human approval alone does not settle that assessment. National consultation rules vary.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish the job's actual scope from an inflated title, challenge inconsistent evaluations and explain difficult pay relativities.

ambition.what: Pre-recruitment job scope and pay-range clinic for hiring managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling descriptions and more time resolving disputed job scope. A delegated right to approve routine description corrections could be added; grade and pay authority remains with the manager unless explicitly changed.

reach.task: Translate a planned vacancy into an accurate role brief.
reach.learn: Structured job interviews, vacancy requirements and how role scope affects recruitment.

reach.task: Check effective-dated salary scale changes before payroll processing.
reach.learn: Pay element mapping, effective dates and retrospective adjustment rules.

evidence.claim: Structured job records, controlled templates and deterministic range calculations can support this workflow; no compensation-specific implementation is documented in the digest.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company has an approved job evaluation framework and reusable description templates.
Benchmark use and derived outputs remain within the data licence.
The tool does not autonomously grade jobs or change employee pay.
Estimates cover a controlled pilot with one job framework and one principal {HCM}; consultation time is elapsed working days.
The structured-input prior fits records and calculations, but interviews and factor judgement remain substantial.
unknowns: Which evaluation framework, collective agreements and benchmark licences apply?
Can the {HCM} accept effective-dated framework changes through approved interfaces?
Who can approve classification changes and salary scales?
Which employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: What validation is appropriate for gender-neutral evaluation factors in the relevant jurisdiction?
Would the intended use place any model component within EU AI Act employment provisions?
new_work: Review generated descriptions against source notes.
Resolve incomplete job facts and benchmark mismatches.
Maintain calculation rules, templates and benchmark versions.
Check publication failures, effective dates and access permissions.

tasks.short: Provide technical liaison on compensation and benefits with employers, public bodies and employee representatives.

steps.what: Locate correspondence, agreements, policy versions and relevant case facts.
Prepare a technical brief covering facts, open questions and the agreed mandate.

loop.input: Authorised source pack and explicit liaison mandate.
loop.output: Referenced brief separating established facts, disputed points and questions.
loop.check: Specialist checks every material assertion, source version and mandate limit.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved conflicts remain flagged for human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Correspondence and agreements express the same issue in varied language and may conflict.

steps.what: Arrange a discussion with the appropriate representatives.
Explain technical issues, hear concerns and discuss possible next steps within the mandate.
Draft the written response and record proposed responsibilities and deadlines.

loop.input: Specialist's discussion notes, referenced brief and proposed follow-up actions.
loop.output: Draft response and action register with unresolved commitments marked.
loop.check: Specialist checks attribution, deadlines, confidentiality and whether any promise exceeds the mandate.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous agreements return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes need interpretation to distinguish concerns, proposals and actual agreements.

steps.what: Approve and send the response, then register confirmed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: An authorised retrieval flow assembles the case pack from the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}; bounded loops draft a referenced brief and follow-up response. The specialist conducts the discussion, while configured scheduling and action tracking use the {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT}. The {EMAIL} sends substantive written commitments only after approval of the exact response.
tasks.previous_blocker: The value lies in trust, interpretation and authority to speak. Earlier tools could store correspondence but could not reliably prepare a case-specific brief.
tasks.enabler_now: Permission-aware retrieval and bounded drafting can reduce preparation and paperwork. Scheduling and action tracking can already be configured without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed interpretations, bargaining and institutional trust remain human. Sensitive correspondence needs purpose-limited access, and national rules determine representative consultation and negotiating authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the counterpart's concerns, explain uncertainty honestly and know when a technical discussion is becoming a negotiation.

ambition.what: Pre-consultation technical issue clinic for employee representatives.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week in substantive discussions and less assembling papers. The tool grants no additional negotiating or commitment authority; that must remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Prepare a joint issue register before a representative consultation.
reach.learn: Consultation procedure, bargaining mandates and how to distinguish clarification from commitment.

reach.task: Assess when a technical issue needs formal escalation.
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds, stakeholder interests and decision authority.

evidence.claim: Retrieval, controlled drafting and action tracking can support liaison work; the digest provides no direct liaison implementation case.
The conversation remains the largest time component; preparation savings do not imply automation of negotiation.

assumptions: The specialist normally works within an agreed liaison mandate.
Scheduling may send neutral invitations to selected contacts without disclosing the case pack.
Discussion notes are written by the specialist; recording or transcription is not assumed.
The relationship-heavy prior is retained, while preparation and follow-up remain open to automation.
Build estimates cover a pilot with selected authorised folders and one shared case process.
unknowns: Which counterpart relationships and types of commitments fall within the specialist's mandate?
Which cases require legal review or manager approval?
Where are authoritative agreements and correspondence stored?
Which national consultation rules and confidentiality arrangements apply?
research_questions: What confidentiality and retention rules apply to representative and government correspondence in the relevant jurisdiction?
new_work: Check source references and identify outdated agreements.
Review drafts for unintended commitments and inaccurate attribution.
Maintain authorised contacts, mandate limits and escalation rules.
Resolve missed deadlines and failed action-register updates.

tasks.short: Model compensation costs and workforce scenarios to support collective bargaining and related decisions.

steps.what: Agree the scenarios, population, time horizon and assumptions with the bargaining team.
Export workforce, pay and employer-cost data for the agreed reference period.
Reconcile populations, pay elements and totals before establishing the baseline.
Translate proposal clauses into eligibility, timing and cost assumptions.
Calculate scenario costs, interactions, sensitivities and impacts by workforce group.
Interpret trade-offs and prepare recommendations with explicit limitations.
Approve the costing pack for use by the bargaining team.

tasks.design: A deterministic costing engine on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins controlled extracts from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {ERP}, reconciles totals and applies versioned scenario rules. It generates sensitivity tables and a {BI} view with restricted group breakdowns. Specialists interpret clauses and trade-offs, and the manager approves the pack in the {DOCS} before bargaining use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pay elements, workforce definitions and employer-cost rules differ across systems. Reusable models are difficult to maintain when proposals change and reconciliation lives in separate workbooks.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can make a small, testable calculation engine and data adapters cheaper to build. Calculations and scenario comparisons require no model loop once specialists specify the rules.
tasks.still_hard: Clause interpretation, behavioural responses and future workforce changes remain uncertain. A correct calculation can still rest on poor assumptions; sensitive group analysis also needs lawful access and disclosure controls.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful assumptions, expose uncertainty and explain why an affordable aggregate proposal may affect workforce groups differently.

ambition.what: Compare the marginal cost of each material proposal revision during bargaining preparation.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time rebuilding workbooks and more time challenging assumptions and distributional effects. They could gain delegated authority to run additional scenarios within agreed assumptions; bargaining commitments and budget approval stay with authorised leaders.

reach.task: Reconcile modelled pay changes against payroll treatment.
reach.learn: Employer contributions, pay element dependencies and retrospective payment handling.

reach.task: Compare the cost implications of alternative agreement clauses.
reach.learn: Bargaining priorities, clause interpretation and acceptable negotiating assumptions.

evidence.claim: Versioned arithmetic, reconciliation and sensitivity analysis are deterministic engineering tasks; the digest provides no direct collective-bargaining costing case.
Estimated savings depend on stable mappings and reusable rules; the proposed time reductions have not been measured.

assumptions: The first release covers one principal payroll jurisdiction and a defined set of pay elements.
Proposal clauses are translated into rules by qualified specialists.
No model predicts individual employee behaviour or decides employee pay.
Structured inputs support the prior, but reconciliation and rule interpretation remain distinct work.
Build ranges include historical comparison, boundary cases and a parallel pilot; consultation is elapsed working days.
unknowns: Which pay elements, contribution rules and collective agreements must be modelled?
Can workforce and payroll records be reconciled through stable identifiers?
Which assumptions and workforce breakdowns may the bargaining team see?
Which historical scenarios are available for independent validation?
research_questions: Which current national contribution rules and agreement interpretations require specialist verification?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions before accepting a baseline.
Maintain pay element mappings and effective-dated cost rules.
Validate new proposal types against independently calculated examples.
Track assumption changes and restrict access to sensitive scenario breakdowns.

tasks.short: Develop, administer and evaluate performance, employment equity and labor relations programs.

steps.what: Gather program participation, completion and workforce outcome records.
Analyse participation gaps, process failures and differences in outcomes.
Draft program options, procedures, responsibilities and evaluation criteria.

loop.input: Approved objectives, diagnostic findings, existing policy and program template.
loop.output: Draft options and procedures with source references and unresolved policy choices.
loop.check: Specialist checks feasibility and fairness; legal questions are referred for qualified review.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unsupported policy choices remain for human decision.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tailoring procedures requires synthesising narrative policy and diagnostic findings; templates alone leave substantial writing.

steps.what: Consult managers and employee representatives, then resolve concerns about the proposed program.
Approve program policy and confirm that required consultation has concluded.
Configure forms, access, deadlines and approval routes for the approved program.
Launch the cycle, send reminders and track outstanding forms and approvals.
Handle disputed outcomes, accessibility needs and exceptions with affected employees and managers.
Evaluate program outcomes and recommend changes for the next cycle.

tasks.design: Controlled integrations from the {HCM} and {TALENT} feed a {BI} dashboard of participation, process and aggregate outcome measures, with small-group disclosure controls. A bounded loop drafts procedures from approved sources in the {DOCS}; people design the policy, consult representatives and approve its use. Configured workflows in the {HCM}, {TALENT} or {WORKFLOW} manage forms and reminders, while disputed outcomes and policy changes remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program rules and responsibilities cross several teams. Existing systems automate cycles, but fragmented records, disputed measures and consultation requirements limit broader automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow configuration can handle routine administration. AI coding can reduce the effort of connecting records and building aggregate reports; bounded drafting helps prepare procedures.
tasks.still_hard: Outcome differences do not establish discrimination or causation. Protected-characteristic data needs a lawful basis and strict access; GDPR, EU AI Act intended-use assessment and national employment and consultation rules must shape the design.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise procedural unfairness, hear contested experiences and choose interventions that employees and managers can use in practice.

ambition.what: Select a quarterly corrective action for persistent program participation gaps.

tasks.altitude: The specialist shifts from chasing forms toward testing program effectiveness and resolving difficult cases. A delegated right to adjust reminder timing and support materials could improve delivery; eligibility, appraisal standards and individual outcomes retain their existing approval routes.

reach.task: Design targeted manager training for recurring appraisal process failures.
reach.learn: Learning needs analysis, accessible training design and evaluation of behaviour change.

reach.task: Investigate whether a program creates unequal access or adverse outcomes.
reach.learn: Fair comparison groups, evidence limits and confidential handling of employee concerns.

reach.task: Prepare and document employee representative consultation on program changes.
reach.learn: National consultation procedures and how to record unresolved objections.

evidence.claim: Cycle configuration, reminders and aggregate reporting are established system patterns; the digest provides no direct case for this proposed HR program.
The proposed model drafts program documents; it does not evaluate individual workers or determine their employment outcomes.

assumptions: The specialist contributes to these programs with the human resources manager and labor relations specialist.
Employment equity is interpreted under applicable European and national rules; no quota-based program is assumed.
Only lawfully held data is used; protected characteristics are not inferred.
The pilot covers one program cycle and aggregate process measures.
The workflow-heavy prior fits administration, but consultation, policy choice and individual disputes remain substantial.
Consent and access estimates include employee consultation where applicable; formal processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which programs and jurisdictions are in scope?
Which representative consultation or consent processes are required?
Which workforce attributes are lawfully available and sufficiently complete for analysis?
What program configuration and access controls already exist in the {HCM} and {TALENT}?
Who decides individual appeals and approves policy changes?
research_questions: Which national rules govern employment equity analysis and representative consultation?
Would any proposed extension into worker evaluation change the EU AI Act classification?
new_work: Review draft procedures and maintain approved source versions.
Check aggregate measures, missing data and small-group disclosure controls.
Test workflow changes before activation and resolve routing failures.
Handle employee concerns and distinguish process problems from substantive disputes.
Reassess program outcomes and maintain metric definitions without treating correlation as causation.

role.altitude: The role moves toward job evaluation, scenario interpretation, consultation and program effectiveness as preparation and administration shrink. New decision rights require explicit delegation; the tools themselves grant none.
reach: Work with payroll clerks to validate effective-dated compensation changes and cost rules.
Work with labor relations specialists to connect technical evidence to consultation and bargaining preparation.
Work with training specialists and equal opportunity representatives to turn program findings into practical interventions.
skills_to_grow: Gender-neutral job evaluation and benchmark matching.
Versioned cost modelling, reconciliation and sensitivity analysis.
Source verification and review of bounded model drafts.
Employment data governance and aggregate disclosure control.
Consultation, facilitation and explanation of uncertain evidence.
Workflow configuration, acceptance testing and exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a reusable reward decision service: job scope clinics, validated bargaining scenarios and quarterly program diagnostics. Each service produces traceable evidence and clear options for the person authorised to decide.

job.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
